entries.claim: `status` unconditionally selects `runs.notes`, but its read-only store open does not run `bring_forward`, so it is incompatible with stores created by the previous schema.
entries.failure_scenario: Run `terminus status` or `terminus status --json` against an existing pre-upgrade store before any writable command has opened it. The `runs` table lacks `notes`, and because the read-only open skips migration, this query fails with `no such column: notes` instead of reporting status. The reader must either tolerate the absent column or ensure an appropriate writable upgrade occurs before querying it.

counter_evidence.note: status opens with Store::open, not open_read_only, and Store::open runs bring_forward on every open of an existing store (crates/terminus-core/src/store/open.rs:193, whose comment names status), so runs.notes exists before the SELECT. No other reader selects runs.notes.
